text.p: SEPT Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA40
LIFFE coffee futures are testing their lowest early June support level of $1,695 basis September, which if broken could start a swift move to $1,600, technical analysts said on Friday.
The market is due to open $20 lower following New York's sharp retracement on Thursday after rising for two days in a row, traders said.
Trevor Neil, a senior technical analyst at Union Cal Futures, said a break below the key $1,695 support would be very bearish.
"It should start a swift move down to $1,600," he said.
"Only a close above $1,850 would relieve the pressure," he added.
The next significant resistance after $1,850 would be $2,040, last seen in May.
Coffee rallied sharply since early January to hit a twin peak at $2,700 in late May from a low of $1,203 in January.
It has fallen since to hover at around $1,800 level currently.
New York arabica futures came under fund liquidation on Thursday as the Brazilian frost fears subsided.
In its commentary on Friday, broker GNI said the odds of a frost from here on were around 20:1, rising to 63:1 by the end of the month and 100:1 just five days after that.
"Clearly frost premium should be eroding rapidly, and the current warm conditions are allowing this year's harvest to continue apace," it said.
